problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x,0,yz⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=y-{x}^{2}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨z,0,0⟩,\,∇f=⟨-2x,1,0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(0,2,-1).$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Curl of a Vector Field Using the Product Rule
examples.problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F(x,y,z) =  \langle 0, y-z, x-y\rangle$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z) = x+y.$ Given that

$$
\nabla\times \mathbf F = \langle 0,\,-1,\,0\rangle, 
\quad
\nabla f = \langle 1,\, 1,\, 0\rangle,
$$

calculate $\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F)$ at the point $(-1,1,3).$
examples.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
\nabla\times(f\,\mathbf F) = f \nabla \times \mathbf {F}+   \nabla f \times \mathbf F
$$

First, we compute $\nabla f \times \mathbf F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & y-z & x-y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (y-z)]\,i-[1\cdot (x-y)-0\cdot (0)]\,j+[1\cdot (y-z)-1\cdot (0)]\,k \\  & =(x-y)\,i+(y-x)\,j+(y-z)\,k \\  & =⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x+y)⟨0,-1,0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-(x+y),0⟩+⟨x-y,\,y-x,\,y-z⟩ \\  & =⟨x-y,\,-2x,\,y-z⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(-1,1,3) & =⟨(-1)-1,\,-2(-1),\,1-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2,\,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Calculate $∇\times (F-2G)$ at the point $(2,\frac{\pi }{2},-1)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=xy\,i+xz\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,k,\,(∇\times G)(x,y,z)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i-x\,k.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following linearity properties for curl:

- $∇\times (kF)=k∇\times F$

- $∇\times (F+G)=∇\times F+∇\times G$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-2G) & =∇\times F-∇\times (2G) \\  & =∇\times F-2∇\times G\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\times F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \frac{∂}{∂x} & \frac{∂}{∂y} & \frac{∂}{∂z} \\ xy & xz & \operatorname{cos}⁡y\end{aligned}| \\  & =[\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz)]i-[\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡y)-\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy)]j+[\frac{∂}{∂x}(xz)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)]k \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)i-(0-0)j+(z-x)k \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)\,i+(z-x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (F-2G) & =∇\times F-2∇\times G \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)\,i+(z-x)\,k-2[-\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i-x\,k] \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)\,i+(z-x)\,k+2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,i+2x\,k \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡y-x)\,i+(z+x)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating at the point $(2,\frac{\pi }{2},-1),$ we get

$$
(∇\times (F-2G))(2,\frac{\pi }{2},-1)=-\,i+k.
$$
